skill.name: seedance-v2
skill.description: Guides generation of short-form videos with ByteDance Seedance 2.0 Pro through the RunComfy CLI. It covers input schema, reference media, lip-sync prompts, model routing, and operational limits.
skill.summary: Create short Seedance 2.0 Pro video jobs for RunComfy with clear prompts and input limits.
skill.author: doany-ai

security_audit.summary: No prompt injection or malware intent was found in SKILL.md. The confirmed risks are disclosed RunComfy CLI commands and one documented outbound model API endpoint; most high filesystem findings are false positives from placeholder URLs or documented token storage.

remediation.issue: The skill asks users or agents to run npm, npx, and RunComfy CLI commands.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running these commands, and pin trusted CLI sources where possible.

remediation.issue: Prompts and media references are submitted to the RunComfy model API.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before sending private media, credentials, customer data, or confidential prompts to the service.

remediation.issue: RunComfy authentication depends on a local token file or RUNCOMFY_TOKEN.
remediation.suggestion: Document token revocation, least-privilege account use, and secure secret handling for CI environments.

content.user_title: Generate Seedance 2.0 Pro Videos on RunComfy
content.value_statement: Short video prompts often need clear schema choices and model routing. This skill guides Seedance 2.0 Pro CLI jobs with reference media, audio, and limits.
actual_capabilities: Documents the RunComfy endpoint and CLI command for bytedance/seedance-v2/pro.
Explains supported inputs for prompts, media references, duration, resolution, audio, aspect ratio, and seed.
Provides text-only, lip-sync, and multimodal command examples.
Gives prompt guidance for camera motion, identity references, and audio tone.
Lists endpoint limits, exit codes, and a troubleshooting reference.
Describes token storage, outbound endpoints, and the generated file size cap.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and network access.
The endpoint is limited to 4 to 15 second clips and up to 720p.
Media references must be hosted URLs within the listed duration and size limits.
Lip-sync and identity consistency depend on reference quality and prompt clarity.

use_cases.title: Create short dialogue ads
use_cases.description: Use a character image and script to plan a 4 to 15 second lip-synced vertical ad.

use_cases.title: Plan cinematic previews
use_cases.description: Combine image, video, and audio references into one concise Seedance shot plan.

use_cases.title: Prepare reliable CLI jobs
use_cases.description: Map user requests to RunComfy inputs, output paths, limits, and retry expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Text-only video prompt
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple short-form video.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Seedance 2.0 Pro prompt for a 5 second 9:16 product teaser. Include camera motion, lighting, mood, and audio direction.

prompt_templates.title: Lip-synced spokesperson ad
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request using one character image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Seedance lip-sync job using this character image and script. Keep the identity stable and describe the voice tone clearly.

prompt_templates.title: Multimodal reference shot
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with image, video, and audio references.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Seedance shot plan from these references. Explain which details belong in media inputs and which belong in the text prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a production request
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before running a RunComfy job.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Seedance request for schema fit, media limits, aspect ratio risks, privacy concerns, and RunComfy execution steps.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a cafe spokesperson ad using one character photo.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends Seedance 2.0 Pro, a 9:16 frame, an 8 second duration, a warm dialogue prompt, and user confirmation before RunComfy execution.

output_examples.input: A team provides image, video, and voice references for a short film preview.
output_examples.output: The skill separates stable identity into image references, motion context into video references, and tone into audio references before preparing the job.

output_examples.input: A user asks why a requested 30 second clip will not work.
output_examples.output: The skill explains the 15 second endpoint limit and suggests splitting the concept into multiple shorter Seedance clips.

best_practices: Ask for explicit confirmation before running RunComfy commands or sending private media to the API.
Put stable identity and brand details in reference images instead of long text descriptions.
Keep clips within 4 to 15 seconds and match reference aspect ratios to the target output.
anti_patterns: Do not run npm, npx, or RunComfy commands without checking the user intent and environment.
Do not include secrets, customer data, or private media in prompts or reference URLs.
Do not ask Seedance for clips longer than 15 seconds in one job.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides Seedance 2.0 Pro video generation through the RunComfy CLI, including prompts, inputs, limits, and troubleshooting.

faq.question: Does it require a RunComfy account?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill requires the RunComfy CLI and either an interactive login or a RUNCOMFY_TOKEN value.

faq.question: Can it create videos longer than 15 seconds?
faq.answer: No. This endpoint supports 4 to 15 second clips. Longer scenes should be split into multiple jobs.

faq.question: Does it send data to a third party?
faq.answer: Yes. Prompts and media references are submitted to RunComfy for model processing after the user approves execution.

faq.question: Can it use reference media?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents up to 9 image references, 3 video references, and 3 audio references.

faq.question: Is lip-sync guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. Lip-sync quality depends on prompt clarity, reference quality, speech content, and model behavior.
